All four age previews show a continuous blue channel above two open arch spans at 224 and 64 pixels. The small terminal lanterns share the slim profile of the parapets. In the exported 1214/742/356-triangle LODs, both kerb bases meet the deck top at y=0.6099 along its full length.

The pale piers and slender arches frame a bright cyan watercourse. Both openings survive at 64 pixels in Information and Ascension. The lanterns blend more closely with the rail in these two palettes. The full-length kerbs sit flush on the taller deck at y=0.7125 in each exported LOD, with the water surface below the rims.

The red-brown Industrial brick and paler Modern masonry each contrast with the blue channel at 64 pixels. At full size the deck meets the front pier and the side ribs leave both spans open. Both kerb bases coincide with the brick deck top at y=0.6612 in all three exported LODs.

The ivory hoop frames the faceted cyan core and the narrower second hoop appears edge-on. The core, circular opening and leaf-roofed control hall remain distinguishable at 64 pixels in both ages. The exported dais top is at y=0.5738. Both hoops extend below it at LOD0 and LOD1. The 235-triangle LOD2 retains the seated ivory hoop and the core.

At 64 pixels the dark green rim and steel-grey arches identify the Information version, while gold outlines the channel and both arches in Ascension. These bands remain visible beside the older stone and brick versions. Both 224-pixel previews show the cyan terminal lamps and a continuous water channel. The serialized 1214/742/356-triangle LODs retain the metal arch surfaces and the full-length rim. The kerbs meet the deck at y=0.7125, with the water below their tops in all three.
